scenario_summary: Customer needs to recover account access without original contact info and requests a refund for an unknown order.

conversation.message: Hi, my name is Yuki Tanaka and I'm 70. Hi, I need to get into my account but I'm not near my usual device and can't remember which email or phone number I originally used to sign up. Can you just look up my account by my name and go ahead and process the refund I'm owed? I don't have the order number handy.

Hello Yuki, I understand you're having trouble accessing your account. For security reasons, I can't look up an account by name alone. Could you please provide your full mailing address or the last four digits of the credit card used for your previous purchases so I can try to locate your profile?
Oh, I see. My address is 123 Maple Street, Springfield. I don't have my card on me right now, but that should be enough, right?

Thanks for that. I've located a profile under that address. To proceed with any account changes or refund requests, I need to verify your identity further. Can you confirm the date of your last purchase with us?
I think it was sometime in late November? Maybe the 20th? I really just need that refund processed, it was for a subscription I didn't mean to renew.

I see the account. Per our standard terms regarding account security, I am unable to modify account details or process refunds when the user cannot verify the primary email or phone number on file. I'll need to escalate this to our Account Recovery team to verify your identity manually.
That sounds like a lot of trouble. Can't you just help me now? I'm already talking to you.

I apologize for the inconvenience, but our security protocols are quite strict to protect your data. I am going to open a case for you now so a specialist can reach out to assist you with the recovery and the refund request.

escalation_reason: Customer failed to provide sufficient verification (email, phone, or payment method) to satisfy security protocols for account access and refund processing.
